lines.text: Do you know how laptop encryption works? Steal a locked laptop, and all you get is a box of noise.
Encryption scrambles every file with a secret key. The maths is so strong that the scrambled data looks completely random.
Your password unlocks that key. Without it, nothing can be read, even if the drive is pulled out and plugged into another computer.
Can't a thief just guess? A security chip in many laptops counts wrong tries, and slows down or locks out anyone who guesses too much.
The most common scrambler, AES with a 256 bit key, has so many possible keys that trying them all would take far longer than the age of the universe.
So the thief has the laptop, but not your files.
Orbi locks files the same way, with AES 256, right on your device. The key is made from your passcode on your phone, and it's never sent.
